title: OAuthFlow
description: Subscription-connect flow state. RUNTIME-DECLARED presentation (S1 gap ③): the server declares what to show and what it expects back; the UI renders declaratively and never keys off a vendor→form table. UI shell semantics mirror the existing BackendOAuthPanel (2s poll, 15-min timeout, cancel). Forms A/B/C from spec §5 frame 09 are presentation patterns the declaration composes: A = auth_url + expects paste_code; B = auth_url + device_code + expects none; C = auth_url + expects paste_callback_url. Under Option 1, native_cli subscription connect drives the CLI's own login through this same shape.
$comment: Owner-approved channel class audit: this is the user-facing presentation wire, not the service-side OAuthFlowState seam. `credential_ref`, `retained_material_disposition`, and `retained_credential_ref` are deliberately excluded because only the service repair consumer acts on them; no UI or wire consumer does. Both channel branches still expose `channel`, and source-bound create/reauth flows carry `source_id`. Evidence at master 05f72ae5: core/handlers/model_hub/native_oauth.py:252-289 produces native success with no engine credential ref, while the HTTP projection publishes presentation fields rather than adapter refs.

intent.description: v2 (07-29, review round 6), extended by the channel class pass: what this flow is FOR, and therefore what its terminal success response carries — `create` → `{flow, source, adopted_by, skipped_by}`, `reauth` → `{flow, source, recovered, interrupted_pairs}` (api.md → OAuth completion responses). Round 5 defined neither, which left the two creation paths inconsistent: `POST /sources` closed the 「so what now?」 loop with an adoption result while the OAuth door — the default way a subscription is added — returned only flow state. Declared as a field rather than inferred, for two reasons. `source_id` cannot discriminate: both channel branches and both intents bind a pending or existing source. And the alternative — the client remembering which button it pressed — makes the response shape a function of client state instead of of the payload, which is exactly how a poll that arrives after a page reload ends up parsed as the wrong shape. OPTIONAL here, REQUIRED at the API boundary from v2 on (README → required-vs-optional): the shipped flow payloads are validated against this file by tests/test_model_hub_api.py and predate the field, so a `required` would fail the contract gate instead of tightening it.

source_id.description: v1.1: pending Source this flow binds to (deterministic association). Both hub and native_cli Model Hub create/reauth flows set it; null remains legal only for legacy presentation payloads.

channel.description: where the resulting credential will live; hub-held subscriptions only behind the consent-gated experimental flag (S2)
